newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks start month with new record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks start month with new record close.

text.p: The Mexican stock market closed at a record high Tuesday, boosted by falling U.S. interest rates and expectations for a rise in Mexican rates.
The blue-chip IPC index rose 50.82 points, or 1.14 percent, to 4,508.79.
On the broad market, gainers outpaced sliders by 63 to 26 out of a total 116 stocks that traded. Volume was heavy at 111.7 million shares.

"Rationally, one would expect to see profit-taking after the run we've had, but the local interest rate outlook has changed a lot over the last couple of days," said Lars Schonander, head of research at Santander Investment Mexico.
"What this is telling you is there is no evidence of pre-election jitters," he added.

Nine money market traders surveyed by Reuters shortly before the central bank closed bidding predicted an average rise of .18 percentage point on bellwether 28-day Cetes, or Mexican treasury bonds, at Tuesday evening's central bank auction.
Dealers had forecast hikes of up to 3 percentage points in Cetes rates Monday.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury rose 18/32, or $5.625 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield to 6.74 percent from 6.79 percent Monday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Mexico will hold elections on July 6 to renew the entire lower house of Congress, one-quarter of the Senate, six state governors and a historic direct vote for Mexico City mayor.
"The market is very strong, secondary interest rates have fallen sharply, a lot of foreigners are in the market again. They seem to be buying ahead of smooth elections," a desk trader said.

"We are also seeing certain repositioning ahead of expected good second-quarter numbers in (construction company) Ara, (construction company) Hogar, some retailers and (steelmaker) Tamsa," Schonander aadded.
Retailer Cifra gained 20 centavos (2.5 cents) to 15.00 pesos ($1.89) in brisk dealing. Tamsa rose 6.70 pesos (84 cents) to 152.50 pesos ($19.23).
Consorcio Ara gained 55 centavos (7 cents) to 28.50 pesos ($3.59), while Consorcio Hogar rose 46 centavos (6 cents) to 11.80 pesos ($1.49).
Dealers said financial stock Bancomer and telecommunications company Telmex drove the market.

Bancomer A series, up 12 centavos (1.5 cents) to 2.42 pesos (31 cents), was the most heavily traded stock for the day, closely followed by its B shares, which ended up 9 centavos (1 cents) to 3.91 pesos (49 cents). The two series together accounted for 21 percent of all shares traded.
"The spread between Bancomer A and B shares is absurdly wide," Schonander said.
Telmex climbed 20 centavos (2.5 cents) to 19.22 pesos ($2.42), while its American Depository Receipts ended up 62. cents at $48.375.
Traders said Telmex ADRs advanced on the back of the Dow Jones industrial average, which closed up 49.54 points at 7,722.33 points.
